[engine] Before attributing ANY single-shot throughput difference, measure the repeatability floor of the SAME binary on the same machine: run it twice and take the spread. If the effect you are attributing is smaller than that spread, the comparison has no discriminating power and the correct output is 'not resolvable', not 'direction unknown'. An instrument whose noise exceeds the signal is not a weak instrument, it is a non-instrument.

**class**: `measurement-hygiene`

## 為什麼（because）

§3 of the whitepaper listed a 6-12% deficit of the rebuilt binary against an 18:00 run of an older one, honestly flagged as unquotable for want of an interleaved A/B -- a framing that implicitly assumed the gap needed explaining. Two runs of the IDENTICAL binary 34 minutes apart (22:30 and 23:04, no rebuild in between: libggml-metal and llama-server both timestamped 22:14) produced tg@0 8.67 -> 6.91 (-20.3%), pp@1024 79.88 -> 105.71 (+32.3%), pp@4096 81.52 -> 103.11 (+26.5%) and tg@512 6.72 -> 8.85 (+31.7%), with per-cell ± as large as the effect (pp@512 ±12.65 on 103.25). So the quantity §3 was comparing across builds moves by up to 32% with nothing changed at all, which makes the 6-12% not merely unquotable but unmeasurable by that method. The two runs also disagree on pool behaviour (hit 97.1%/519501 reads vs 97.3%/16163 misses), so it is not only the timing that drifts between launches.

## 反例（counterexample_observed）

The same binary, unmodified, two consecutive runs: tg@0 8.67 vs 6.91 t/s.
